final_candidates.decision_summary: N301 anchors the V3 glycan-loop; altering this site perturbs V3-directed antibody recognition while leaving the surrounding glycan shield largely intact. S conserves local polarity, limiting folding risk.

N390 is a V3-proximal N-linked glycan site frequently implicated in escape from glycan-dependent neutralizing antibodies. A serine substitution preserves local character better than alanine, reducing fitness cost.

Loss of the N337 glycan site is associated with resistance to some glycan-dependent broadly neutralizing antibodies and is tolerated in many Env backgrounds. Fitness cost is uncertain but generally moderate.

stop_reason.detail: LLM-only iterative control with no external evidence; one self-review round completed and further rounds are unlikely to improve the Top-3.

history.rationale: Disrupts the N301-N303 PNG site at the V3 base (verified N301 followed by T303), which is a key contact for PGT121/PGT128/PGT135-family bNAbs; glycan-hole loss here is a common fitness-retaining escape route.

N301 is a well-established V3 glycosylation-loop position; removing/altering it shifts V3 exposure and can reduce neutralization by V3-directed antibodies while the surrounding glycan shield remains intact.

Removes the N337-E338-T339 PNG site (verified N337 followed by T339) in the C3/V3 stem, reducing neutralization by glycan-V3-dependent antibodies; partial compensation from neighboring glycans (N301, N390) limits fitness cost.
Loss of the N337 glycan site is associated with resistance to some glycan-dependent broadly neutralizing antibodies and is tolerated in many Env backgrounds.

Disrupts the N390-S391 PNG site (verified N390 followed by S391) in the V3-adjacent glycan cluster, an escape route for PGT128-like and 2G12-like bNAbs while other glycans maintain the outer-domain shield.

N390 is a V3-loop-proximal N-linked glycan site frequently implicated in antibody escape, so it is slightly more attractive than initially ranked; a S substitution preserves local character better than A.

N187 lies in the V2 region (verified N at position 187 within the NRSNNSN motif); altering this Asn cluster perturbs strand-antibody contact in the V1V2 apex region without introducing a cysteine or proline that would destabilize folding.
N187 glycan participates in the V1V2 glycan cluster recognized by apex antibodies; deleting it can disrupt those epitopes, though folding risk is moderate.

K162 (verified Lys at position 162 in QKVYSL) sits in V2; substitution to Asn can modulate strand-based V1V2-apex bNAb (PG9/PGDM1400-class) recognition and may create a compensatory sequon context in adjacent residues, though fitness impact is uncertain.
This mutation creates an artificial glycan rather than removing one; gain-of-glycan at the V2 apex is a known escape mechanism, but prediction of correct NXS/T occupancy is uncertain.
